To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the side-channel attacks and the fault attacks are the most important physical attacks for the cryptographic systems and that the complexity evaluation of the successful attacks is the most important issue for their countermeasure development.
side-channel attacks and physical attacks are the most important and most effective methods to attack cryptographic devices.
the complexity analysis of the key recovery is essential for side-channel and fault attacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the security evaluation of the cryptographic devices and protocols.
the following two questions: (1) How accurate is the key recovery of side-channel attacks?
the following three topics: (1) the side-channel attacks and their countermeasures, (2) the fault attacks and their countermeasure, (3) the complexity evaluation for physical attacks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the key recovery is possible with the polynomial-time complexity for both side-channel attacks and the fault attacks.
the complexity of these physical attacks is the same as that of the brute-force attack.

the complexity evaluation of these attacks should take the statistical analysis of the information leakage into account, and it should be the statistical analysis that determines the success of the attacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complexity evaluation of the side-channel attacks is still an open problem.

the complexity of the key recovery for side-channel attacks and that for fault attacks are the same, and the complexity is the same as that for brute-force attacks, which is the complexity of exhaustive key search.
we have developed a unified framework for the complexity evaluation for both side-channel attacks and differential fault analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of side-channel attacks and the fault attacks can be estimated by the number of the secret bits.
the complexity of side-channel attacks and the complexity of fault attacks can be evaluated by the number of the required measurements and the number of the necessary fault injections, respectively.
, in order to evaluate the security of a system, we need to take into account the complexity of both the attack itself and the defense mechanisms.
